# Visual audit and revision

## Plot question

How does mean BMI differ across NHANES cycles for adults age 20-80 in each income group in the classroom NHANES equity dataset?

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Data used for the final figure

```{r}
#| label: final-summary
plot_data <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80,
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(IncomeGroup),
    !is.na(Cycle)
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle, IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(Cycle = factor(Cycle, levels = sort(unique(Cycle))))

plot_data
```

## Corrected plot

```{r}
#| label: corrected-plot
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
final_plot <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, color = IncomeGroup, group = IncomeGroup)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(26, 31.5),
    breaks = seq(26, 31, by = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean BMI by income group across NHANES cycles",
    subtitle = "Adults age 20-80 in the classroom NHANES equity dataset",
    x = "NHANES cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI",
    color = "Income group",
    caption = "Descriptive, unweighted classroom summary. Missing BMI, income group, and cycle values were excluded."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, lineheight = 1.2, margin = margin(t = 12)),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10, b = 22, l = 10)
  )

final_plot

ggsave(
  file.path("assignments", "assignment05-visualization", "submission", "corrected-plot.png"),
  final_plot,
  width = 9,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Why the revision is more honest

The original flawed version used a clipped y-axis and a causal title, which overstated the size of the difference and implied a stronger conclusion than the descriptive summary can support. The revised version keeps the full BMI range in view, uses a neutral title, and reports the analysis as a descriptive, unweighted classroom comparison. The figure still shows the clear pattern that lower-income adults have higher mean BMI than higher-income adults across almost every cycle, but it does not present that pattern as proof of a causal relationship.

## Final caption

Descriptive, unweighted classroom summary. Mean BMI among adults age 20-80 is shown by NHANES cycle and income group in the prepared NHANES equity dataset (source: examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv). Missing BMI, income group, and cycle values were excluded; no survey weights were applied, so this is a descriptive comparison rather than a weighted national estimate or causal analysis.
